ruling: OPTION (a). It IS a collision: change_id is ONE GLOBAL namespace, not a per-file one, because WRITE_RULES.md section 5 step 2 requires a duplicate check before writing and because every citation in bible/ and qa/ is written as a bare 'BIB-NNNN' with no file qualifier - a per-file scope would make those citations unresolvable. The tie is broken by the register: bible/changelog.md is where an id is actually allocated, so the entry already logged there (task p4-h2-bible) KEEPS BIB-0029, and the creature.json amendment (task p4-h2-creature), which never reached the changelog, moves to the next free number BIB-0032 and receives the changelog entry it was missing (WRITE_RULES.md P-011, retroactive record of a domain agent's own fix-write). Verified unique across bible/ and qa/ before writing: BIB-0001..BIB-0031 were in use, so BIB-0032 (this renumber) and BIB-0033 (the SCN-long-hall daylight arbitration in the same task) were free.
gate_file_check: Neither signed gate file cites BIB-0029. runs/g4/gate.json cites only BIB-0027 (three mentions) and runs/g5-ep01/gate.json cites no BIB id at all, so nothing recorded in a signed gate was renumbered.

citations_deliberately_not_updated: runs/p4-h2-creature/result.json, runs/p4-h2-creature/meta.json and runs/dag.json still say BIB-0029. Run receipts are immutable records of what a task wrote at the time and are not rewritten; the redirect is the supersedes field on the BIB-0032 changelog entry - a BIB-0029 citation dated to task p4-h2-creature means BIB-0032.
rule_for_next_parallel_batch: Recorded as precedent P-013 in bible/WRITE_RULES.md: BIB numbers are one global namespace and the changelog is the register, so agents DO NOT self-assign a literal number. Since every write goes through memory-bible anyway (WRITE_RULES.md section 1), the writing agent proposes 'BIB-PENDING' with its task_id and memory-bible stamps the real number at the moment it appends the changelog entry - one writer, one register, no race. An agent writing its own file under a defect (P-011) does the same. Writing a literal number without checking bible/changelog.md first is a section 5 step 2 failure.
